findings.title: DMARC not enforced (p=none): domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud

evidence.excerpt: DMARC record: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@brightwaterfleet.example; policy: none, pct: 100

findings.deal_impact: DMARC at p=none allows domain spoofing attempts to pass, increasing BEC/wire-fraud and phishing risk to customers and counterparties; remediation is usually straightforward but requires mail-flow validation.

remediation.summary: Move DMARC from p=none to quarantine then reject after monitoring rua reports and validating all senders.

findings.title: SPF uses soft/neutral fail

evidence.excerpt: SPF record: v=spf1 include:_spf.mailhost.example include:sendgrid.example ~all; qualifier: ~all, lookup_count: 2

findings.deal_impact: Softfail SPF weakens enforcement against unauthorized senders and compounds the DMARC p=none exposure for spoofing.

remediation.summary: Inventory authorized senders, then change SPF from ~all to -all in coordination with DMARC enforcement.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled

evidence.excerpt: DNSSEC check: queried_name brightwaterfleet.example, record_type DS, enabled: false

findings.deal_impact: Without DNSSEC, DNS responses lack authenticated integrity, modestly increasing spoofing/redirection risk for web and mail services.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC at the registrar/DNS provider and publish DS records, with monitoring for resolution failures.

findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems

evidence.excerpt: Risky hostname vpn.brightwaterfleet.example, pattern vpn, first_seen 2023-02-11, last_seen 2026-09-30
Risky hostname jenkins-old.brightwaterfleet.example, pattern jenkins|old, first_seen 2021-06-03, last_seen 2026-08-14
Risky hostname staging-api.brightwaterfleet.example, pattern staging, first_seen 2024-01-20, last_seen 2026-10-01
Risky hostname legacy-portal.brightwaterfleet.example, pattern legacy, first_seen 2019-11-05, last_seen 2026-07-22; risky_hostnames_count 4

findings.deal_impact: CT-logged VPN, old Jenkins, staging API and legacy portal names signal potentially exposed or poorly retired systems that merit validation in confirmatory diligence; presence alone does not prove they are reachable.

remediation.summary: Validate reachability and ownership of risky hostnames, decommission or restrict legacy/staging/admin systems, and enforce MFA/patching on VPN.

findings.title: Large certificate footprint relative to company size

evidence.excerpt: CT query returned unique_hostnames: 47, risky_hostnames_count: 4 for a 201-1000 employee company

findings.deal_impact: 47 unique hostnames suggests attack-surface sprawl that may include forgotten assets, increasing inventory and patch-management burden post-close.

remediation.summary: Reconcile all 47 CT hostnames to an authoritative asset inventory and remove or consolidate unowned/stale services.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS versions offered

evidence.excerpt: tls_support TLSv1.0: true, TLSv1.1: true, TLSv1.2: true; tls_versions [TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2]

findings.deal_impact: Offering TLS 1.0/1.1 on www weakens transport security and may affect compliance/customer security reviews.

remediation.summary: Disable TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1 on www and other web endpoints, retaining TLS 1.2+.

findings.title: HSTS not set

evidence.excerpt: Headers: strict-transport-security: null on https://brightwaterfleet.example/
Headers: strict-transport-security: null on https://www.brightwaterfleet.example/

findings.deal_impact: Missing HSTS leaves first-visit/downgrade exposure and is a common low-cost gap flagged in customer and insurer security reviews.

remediation.summary: Add Strict-Transport-Security header on apex and www after confirming HTTPS-only operation.

findings.title: Internet-facing appliance listed in CISA KEV (version not verified)

evidence.excerpt: KEV match CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001, vendor ExampleGate, product ExampleGate SSL-VPN, version 7.0.11, match_tier appliance_exposed, match_level product; note: KEV lists products, not affected versions; version not verified. Snapshot 2026-10-20.
Fingerprint product ExampleGate SSL-VPN, version 7.0.11, kind appliance, source asset_path on www host

findings.deal_impact: Potential exposure: an internet-facing ExampleGate SSL-VPN fingerprint matches a CISA KEV-listed product (version not verified), so patch level must be urgently confirmed pre-close as VPN appliances are high-value targets.

remediation.summary: Immediately verify ExampleGate SSL-VPN version/patch against KEV CVE, patch or isolate the appliance, and review for compromise indicators.

findings.title: Publicly disclosed security incident in the last 24 months

evidence.excerpt: State AG breach notice dated 2025-08-14: unauthorized access to a customer support system; approx. 3,100 individuals notified. Entity match exact; disclosed_within_months: 14.

findings.deal_impact: A disclosed breach 14 months ago affecting ~3,100 individuals raises regulatory, notification, litigation and insurability diligence, and requires review of root cause and remediation closure.

remediation.summary: Obtain breach investigation, regulator correspondence and remediation evidence; confirm notification obligations closed and lessons implemented.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.1)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.1 exception: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.2)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.2 exception: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC7.2 exception: For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

remediation.summary: Remediate CC8.1 exception: 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

findings.title: SOC 2 report period ended more than 90 days ago; no bridge letter provided

evidence.excerpt: Report period ended 2026-03-31; 213 days before 2026-10-30.

findings.deal_impact: Report period ended 2026-03-31, 213 days before the assessment date; controls may have changed since.

remediation.summary: Obtain a bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30.

findings.title: Critical subservice organization carved out of SOC 2 scope

evidence.excerpt: Nimbus Cloud Services is carved out of scope: infrastructure hosting.

findings.deal_impact: Nimbus Cloud Services (infrastructure hosting) is carved out of scope and is critical to production or in-scope data.

remediation.summary: Obtain the Nimbus Cloud Services SOC report and assess carve-out risk.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Every admin account is behind MFA. No exceptions. That's been true for years. It's enforced through our conditional access policy.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 CC6.1 exception: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA, bypassing conditional access via a legacy provisioning script. This directly conflicts with 'every admin account, no exceptions.'

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Offboarding is automated. HR flags the termination and access is revoked same day through our identity provider.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 CC6.2 exception: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days, contradicting automated same-day revocation on termination.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We have a 24 7 SOC through our MSSP, every alert gets looked at, nothing sits.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 CC7.2 exception: for 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10-23, 2025) alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed, contradicting that every alert gets looked at.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We're fully locked down there. DMARC is enforced. Nobody can spoof our domain.

contradictions.explanation: DMARC record is v=DMARC1; p=none, policy none. Monitoring-only DMARC does not enforce rejection, so the domain can be spoofed, contradicting 'DMARC is enforced.'

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: No, nothing material. We've never had a breach.

contradictions.explanation: State AG breach notice dated 2025-08-14 reports unauthorized access to a customer support system with approx. 3,100 individuals notified, contradicting 'never had a breach / nothing material.'

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We decommissioned the legacy stuff a while back. Everything external goes through the main app and the VPN.

contradictions.explanation: CT log presence alone doesn't prove a host is live; however certificates for jenkins-old (last_seen 2026-08-14) and legacy-portal (last_seen 2026-07-22) within the last 12 months show these legacy systems are still actively maintained, contradicting decommissioning.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Annual third party test. The last one came back clean. No highs.

contradictions.explanation: Annual independent penetration test control had no exceptions, but the same evidence states 2 high-severity findings were reported in the test. That contradicts 'came back clean. No highs.'

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Daily backups to immutable storage in a second region and we do a restore test every quarter.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 A1.2-01 was tested with no exceptions: production data is backed up daily to immutable storage and restore tests are performed quarterly. This positive tested evidence corroborates the backup and restore-test claim.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We can get one. one we haven't needed it so far.

contradictions.explanation: No bridge letter has been provided and the report period ended 2026-03-31, but SOC 2 Section 5 states management plans to obtain a bridge letter covering April 1, 2026 forward upon request, corroborating that one can be obtained.

deal_recommendations.text: Require verification of the ExampleGate SSL-VPN version and patch status, a compromise assessment, and a bring-down of security representations before signing in Days 0–30 as a closing condition under the full cyber diligence required before signing [F-008].

Commission a scope that technically reviews the KEV-listed SSL-VPN exposure in Days 0–30 and independently validates management representations through Days 31–60 and Days 61–100, reflecting full cyber diligence before signing [F-008] [C-001] [C-005].
Negotiate protection for pre-closing incident losses through a specific indemnity, informed by the incident review in Days 31–60 and by full cyber diligence before signing [F-009].

Assume the known disclosed incident will be excluded from representations and warranties coverage, seek broker confirmation in Days 31–60, and complete full cyber diligence before signing without relying on that coverage for this exposure [F-009].

Confirm cyber insurability and likely underwriting requirements before close, addressing domain-spoofing exposure and the access-control exceptions scheduled for Days 31–60 as part of full cyber diligence before signing [F-001] [F-010] [F-011].

Impose a covenant to complete remaining remediation across Days 31–60, Days 61–100 and After day 100 for access controls, monitoring, change approvals, email authentication, exposed hostnames, transport security, incident closure and the bridge letter, following full cyber diligence before signing [F-010] [F-011] [F-012] [F-001] [F-009] [F-014].

Make no price adjustment on cyber grounds because total remediation of $142K–$643K across Days 0–30 through After day 100 is immaterial relative to the 50M-250M revenue band, while still completing full cyber diligence before signing [F-008] [F-009].

narrative.executive_summary:
Bottom line: Escalate to full cyber diligence before signing for Brightwater Fleet Systems. It is rated D at 56.8, capped by a critical, potentially exploitable exposure [F-008], a publicly disclosed incident within 24 months [F-009], and multiple management statements contradicted by evidence [C-001].
Key risks: The internet-facing ExampleGate SSL-VPN matches a CISA KEV-listed product with version not verified [F-008]. The disclosed incident affected approx. 3,100 individuals [F-009], 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts lacked enforced MFA [F-010], and 3 of 15 terminated users retained access [F-011]. DMARC is not enforced and alerts went unreviewed for 2 consecutive weeks [F-001] [F-012].
Management credibility: Of 9 contradictions, 7 were contradicted and 2 were supported [C-001] [C-005]. Contradictions cover MFA, offboarding, alert review, DMARC enforcement and incident history [C-001] [C-002] [C-003] [C-004] [C-005].
Next steps: Verify the SSL-VPN version and complete a compromise assessment in Days 0–30 before signing [F-008]. Complete incident and access-control diligence in Days 31–60 [F-009] [F-010].
key_questions_for_management: Provide the ExampleGate SSL-VPN version, patch evidence and compromise-assessment results for the KEV-listed appliance [F-008].
Provide the breach investigation, regulator correspondence and remediation-closure evidence for the disclosed incident affecting approx. 3,100 individuals [F-009] [C-005].
Reconcile the claim that every admin account is behind MFA with the 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts not enforced for MFA [F-010] [C-001].
Reconcile the claim of automated same-day offboarding with the 3 of 15 terminated users who retained access for 6, 11, and 19 business days [F-011] [C-002].
Provide evidence that security alerts are now routed, reviewed and escalated following the 2 consecutive weeks when alerts were not reviewed [F-012] [C-003].
Confirm the plan and timetable to move DMARC from monitoring-only to enforcement and to strengthen SPF [F-001] [F-002] [C-004].
Provide the SOC 2 bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30 and the Nimbus Cloud Services SOC report for the carved-out hosting service [F-014] [F-015].
Reconcile the 47 certificate-transparency hostnames to the authoritative asset inventory, including the VPN, old Jenkins, staging API and legacy portal hostnames [F-004] [F-005] [C-006].

limitations: Passive outside-in assessment only; no authenticated or internal testing

exceptions.description: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA.
exceptions.management_response: Management disabled the legacy provisioning script in April 2026 and has begun migrating service-desk accounts to the standard conditional access policy. Migration expected to complete Q3 2026.

exceptions.description: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.
exceptions.management_response: Management is evaluating an automated HR-to-IdP de-provisioning integration. Until then, terminations are processed manually by IT upon email notification from HR.

exceptions.description: For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.
exceptions.management_response: The distribution list was corrected on November 24, 2025. Management has added a weekly check that alert routing is functioning.

exceptions.description: 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).
exceptions.management_response: Management has updated the emergency change procedure to require post-deployment approval within 48 hours.
